info.title: er-server
info.description: Entity Resolution control + read API. Component schemas are generated from the entity definitions (entities/*/entity.yaml) via er-entity-gen; this document is their single serialized form.

AcctGoldenLineage.description: Per-attribute survivorship provenance for a resolved account: which record each surviving value came from.

attribute.description: The survivable attribute decided (e.g. company_name, domain, address).

created_at.description: Run-logical creation time (the assembling run's clock; the mart is rebuilt whole).

entity_id.description: The resolved account this attribute decision belongs to.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('acct_golden_lineage:' || entity_id || ':' || attribute).

record_key.description: The source record that won the attribute.

rule.description: The survivorship rule that selected this value.

source_record_id.description: Source-native id of the winning record.

source_system.description: Source system of the winning record.

survivorship_version.description: Survivorship policy version that produced this row.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time (equals created_at; the mart is rebuilt whole).

AcctGoldenRecord.description: One resolved account/organization: the surviving value per attribute, at a snapshot.

addr_postal.description: Surviving postal code of the address.

created_at.description: Run-logical creation time (the assembling run's clock; the mart is rebuilt whole).

id.description: Persistent entity id (deterministic UUIDv7, minted by reconcile); the survivorship key.

phone_e164.description: Surviving phone number in E.164 form.

survivorship_version.description: Survivorship policy version that produced this row.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time (equals created_at; the mart is rebuilt whole).

ApiKey.description: An org-scoped API key: its role and the at-rest hash of the secret.

id.description: The key's unique id (UUIDv7, minted at issue).

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked, if it has been.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

AuditLog.description: The append-only audit ledger: one row per authenticated mutation (actor, action, optional org scope, and structured detail). Append-only constrains writes, not lifetime: rows past the deployment retention window (ER_AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS, floor 400 days per the infra D-RETENTION decision) are retired by the dispatcher's retention sweep through delete/purge_expired.

actor.description: The principal that performed the action (the signed-in user's email, or an API key id).

created_at.description: Wall-clock creation time (database default; `at` remains the domain event stamp).

dataset.description: The dataset the action concerned, by name, when it concerned one — context, like `org`, not a foreign key (this ledger outlives both).

id.description: Monotonic ledger id (bigserial); the primary key.

org.description: The tenant the action applies to, if the action is org-scoped.

trace_id.description: The W3C trace id (32 lowercase hex) of the request that caused this row, when the caller sent one. The JOIN KEY to the span store: spans carry `trace_id`, so this is what turns `which rows did this session write` into `and here is every SQL statement each one ran`. Stored as the bare id rather than the full `traceparent`, because the parent span id is per-hop and would not join. NULL for an unpropagated or non-HTTP caller — a CLI, the dispatcher's own bookkeeping — which is a real and permanent case, not a gap to backfill.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (equals created_at; audit rows are append-only).

CandidateKey.description: What an equi-join on one column would cost as a blocking key, measured against the corpus rather than inferred from a model. Blocking decides the entire cost of a run, and it is chosen before anything is trained — so the question has to be answerable with no model at all, which is why these numbers come from a GROUP BY over the data and not from a settings document.

covered_rows.description: Rows where every key column is non-null — the only rows this key can block, because an equality is never true of a NULL.

distinct_values.description: Distinct key values among the covered rows. The block count: more blocks of fewer rows each is what makes a key cheap.

entropy_bits.description: Shannon entropy of the key's value distribution, in bits. In bits so it is directly comparable with the compiler's match-weight scale, which is also in bits — one unit across both halves of the system.

expected_pairs.description: Pairs an equi-join on this key generates, exactly: the sum of C(n, 2) over the value groups. For a rule used FIRST, with nothing preceding it to dedup against, this equals the marginal comparison count a trained model's own counter reports — which is what the engine's golden test asserts, so the cheap path cannot drift from the expensive one.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('candidate_keys:' || profile_run_id || ':' || key_columns).

key_columns.description: The key's columns, joined by the unit-separator character (chr(31)) — one name for a single-column key, several for a composite. A delimiter rather than a list because this column is in the natural key, and DuckLake has no list equality to MERGE on; chr(31) specifically because it cannot occur in a column name.

largest_block_pairs.description: Pairs contributed by the single largest block. The number that catches a key which looks affordable in total and is actually dominated by one value — the classic shape being a placeholder, where every record with a blank-but-present field lands in one enormous block.

pair_loss_from_nulls.description: The share of ALL corpus pairs this key can never reach because one endpoint or the other is NULL: `1 - (covered_rows / rows)^2`. The square is the part that surprises people — a key on a column that is 60% populated reaches only 36% of pairs — and it is why a cheap key is so often cheap for the wrong reason. Stored beside the cost so the trade is visible rather than implied.

profile_run_id.description: The profile run that measured this key. Named for the relation it points at, per the foreign-key convention; no `references` is declared because DuckLake enforces no foreign keys (V11).

row_count.description: Rows in the profiled corpus, carried so `expected_pairs` can be read as a share without a second lookup. Named row_count rather than rows because `rows` is reserved in DuckDB and a column called that cannot be selected unquoted.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time.

ColumnProfile.description: One column's shape within one profile run: how full it is, how many distinct values it holds, how long its values are, what types they parse as, and its most frequent values. One row per column rather than per value, because the lake schema language cannot express a partition (there is no partition_by field) and a per-value table would grow with the corpus instead of with the schema.

blank_count.description: Rows where the column is present but empty once trimmed. Counted apart from NULL because ingest lands every delivered value as a JSON string, so an empty cell arrives as '' and is not NULL — a fill rate treating the two alike reports a column as populated when every value in it is blank.

cast_bigint.description: Non-null values that parse as an integer.

cast_boolean.description: Non-null values that parse as a boolean.

cast_date.description: Non-null values that parse as a date. This is the whole of type detection here: ingest stores every delivered value as text, so the declared type says nothing about content and conformance is the only evidence of what a column actually holds.

cast_double.description: Non-null values that parse as a double.

cast_timestamp.description: Non-null values that parse as a timestamp.

column_name.description: The profiled column, as named in the corpus stage.

distinct_approx.description: HyperLogLog estimate of distinct values. Always present because it is cheap, and always approximate: measured on a fixture of 1000 genuinely distinct ids it returns 978, so it is wrong in both directions and must never settle a uniqueness question on its own.

distinct_exact.description: Exact distinct count, NULL when it was not requested. The expensive one (a per-column sort), and the only one a uniqueness verdict may be read from.

distinct_normalized.description: Exact distinct count after lowercasing, trimming and collapsing internal whitespace; NULL when not requested. Materially below distinct_exact is the signal that a column needs standardizing before it is compared, which is otherwise invisible — the raw count looks healthy precisely because the variants are counted as distinct values.

entropy_bits.description: Shannon entropy of the value distribution, in bits. Reported in bits so it is directly comparable with the compiler's match-weight scale, which is also in bits — one unit across both halves of the system. A low value means one or two values dominate, which makes the column a poor blocking key however full it is.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('column_profiles:' || profile_run_id || ':' || column_name).

len_max.description: Longest trimmed value length. A value at a round number here is the signature of upstream truncation.

len_min.description: Shortest trimmed value length. NULL for an all-NULL column, where a length has no meaning.

len_p95.description: Approximate 95th-percentile trimmed length. Read against len_max it separates a long tail from a single outlier.

non_null_count.description: Rows where the column is not NULL.

num_avg.description: Mean of the values that parse as numbers.

num_max.description: Largest value that parses as a number, NULL when none does.

num_min.description: Smallest value that parses as a number, NULL when none does.

num_std.description: Sample standard deviation of the values that parse as numbers. NULL for fewer than two such values, where it is undefined rather than zero.

profile_run_id.description: The profile run this column belongs to. Named for the relation it points at, per the foreign-key convention, but no `references` is declared because DuckLake enforces no foreign keys (V11) and declaring one would claim a guarantee the lake does not provide.

row_count.description: Rows read for this column (the sampled count when sampling was on).

top_values.description: The most frequent values with their counts and shares, bounded to a small k. Bounded because this is a per-column row: an unbounded list would put the corpus inside the profile. NOTE for consumers: these are REAL VALUES — live emails and phone numbers — so they are the one field here that carries personal data and must be role-gated before display and never sent to a model.

total_row_count.description: Rows in the corpus whether or not they were sampled, so a sampled figure can be scaled and labelled honestly.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time.

ConfigVersion.description: A versioned config document for a tenant: its YAML, hash and publish state.

dataset_id.description: The dataset this config version belongs to. Part of the natural key: rows belong to a dataset, not to the org at large.

id.description: The version row's unique id (UUIDv7, minted at draft).

org_id.description: The tenant this config version belongs to.

published_at.description: When the version was published, if it has been.

state.description: Whether the version is a draft or published.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

version.description: The monotonic version number within the tenant.

Dataset.description: One of a tenant's resolution domains: its own lake location, config pointer, entity type and lifecycle state. The lake env points at a DuckLake catalog of its own (a METADATA_SCHEMA inside the org's metadata database, or a file catalog locally), so two datasets never share tables.

active_config_version.description: The currently published config version, if any.

config_path.description: Path to the dataset's config document.

display_name.description: Optional human label; the name stays the stable routing handle.

drop_root.description: Delivery landing directory; one `<source>.csv` per config source.

entity_type.description: The one entity type this dataset's lake resolves. Fixed at creation: the lake's std/golden tables are per-type, so changing it would orphan the corpus. Publish refuses a config whose entity_type differs.

env.description: Lake connection env (catalog, catalog schema, data path, config/model/TF/lexicon paths). Handed to the engine verbatim; the derived location keys always win over operator extras.

id.description: The dataset's unique id (UUIDv7, minted at creation).

name.description: The dataset's name, unique within its org (the routing handle; URLs are name-based, same slug grammar as an org name). The migration sweep names every existing org's one dataset `default`.

org_id.description: The tenant this dataset belongs to.

s3_ingest_bucket.description: Bucket the auto-ingest poller watches for this dataset. Null means auto-ingest is off — the feature has to be opted into, because a poller that starts reading a bucket nobody pointed at it would be ingesting data on its own initiative.

s3_ingest_prefix.description: Key prefix under `s3_ingest_bucket`, with one directory per config source beneath it. A column rather than a key in `env` deliberately, for the same reason as the org's: `env` is handed to the engine subprocess, while this is read by the control plane itself.

state.description: Dataset lifecycle state. The org's own state gates the whole tenant above this.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

EntityLink.description: A relationship between two resolved entities that is NOT a merge: a household, a corporate hierarchy, a 'these are related but distinct' note. The product has one answer to 'these two records belong together' — merge them — and that answer is wrong for a husband and wife at one address, or a subsidiary and its parent. Merging them loses the distinction and no later run can recover it; refusing to record anything loses the relationship. A link records it without collapsing either side.

child_entity_id.description: The entity on the member side — the person in the household, the subsidiary.

created_by.description: The actor that created the link.

dataset_id.description: The dataset whose entities this link relates — entity ids are lake-local.

id.description: The link's unique id (UUIDv7, minted by the application).

kind.description: What the relationship is. A closed set rather than free text because the whole value of a link is that something downstream can act on it, and an export or a rule cannot act on a spelling. `related` is the deliberate escape hatch for a real relationship that is neither of the other two — it says 'these are connected, do not merge them' without claiming to know how.

note.description: Optional free text — why this link exists, in the words of whoever made it.

org_id.description: The tenant. Every read is scoped by it.

origin.description: Where the link came from. Kept apart for the reason `pair_labels.origin` is: a steward's judgement and a model's suggestion are different evidence, and a surface that cannot tell them apart will present a guess as a decision. `llm` has no producer until an adjudicator can propose a link; it is declared here because the column's accepted values are the contract that producer will be written against.

parent_entity_id.description: The entity on the owning side — the household, the parent company. Deliberately NOT a foreign key, for the reason `taggings.subject_id` gives: an entity lives in the LAKE and this table is Postgres, so a database-level reference would point at a row this store does not own. The id is stable across runs because reconcile carries ids forward by membership overlap (INV-PERM) rather than re-deriving them, and an entity that loses that contest records `merged_into` — so a link survives its entity gaining members, and a merged-away side is followable rather than dangling.

updated_at.description: When it was last changed.

GoldenLineage.description: Per-attribute survivorship provenance: which record each surviving golden value came from.

attribute.description: The survivable attribute decided (e.g. given_name, email, address).

created_at.description: Run-logical creation time (the assembling run's clock; the mart is rebuilt whole).

entity_id.description: The resolved entity this attribute decision belongs to.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('golden_lineage:' || entity_id || ':' || attribute).

record_key.description: The source record that won the attribute.

rule.description: The survivorship rule that selected this value.

source_record_id.description: Source-native id of the winning record.

source_system.description: Source system of the winning record.

survivorship_version.description: Survivorship policy version that produced this row.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time (equals created_at; the mart is rebuilt whole).

GoldenRecord.description: One resolved person: the surviving value per attribute, at a snapshot.

addr_number.description: Surviving street number of the address.

addr_postal.description: Surviving postal code of the address.

addr_street.description: Surviving street name of the address.

assembled_at.description: Assembly time of this row (volatile; excluded from determinism comparisons).

created_at.description: Run-logical creation time (the assembling run's clock; the mart is rebuilt whole).

id.description: Persistent entity id (deterministic UUIDv7, minted by reconcile); the survivorship key.

phone_e164.description: Surviving phone number in E.164 form.

survivorship_version.description: Survivorship policy version that produced this row.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time (equals created_at; the mart is rebuilt whole).

IngestBatch.description: One delivery receipt (S4.1): per-source landing counts for a batch, including tombstones and resurrections.

changed_count.description: Rows superseding a key with new content.

full_refresh_keys.description: Whether the delivery tombstoned omitted keys.

id.description: The delivery batch's unique id (caller-supplied per delivery).

matched_count.description: Screening (E9b): delivered records that joined an existing entity — their best active score reached `thresholds.auto_merge`. NULL means the delivery was never screened, which is the honest answer for a run that scored nothing (a correction pass, or a rebuild with `skip_ingest`); 0 means it was screened and nothing matched.

review_count.description: Screening (E9b): delivered records whose best active score landed in the gray band — at or above `review_low` but below `auto_merge`. These are the ones a steward has to decide.

run_id.description: The run that wrote this row.

screened_at.description: When the delivery was screened, NULL if it was not. Separate from the counts so that `screened with everything unmatched` (counts 0/0/N) is distinguishable from `never screened` (all NULL) without reading three columns.

tombstone_count.description: Keys tombstoned by a full refresh.

unchanged_count.description: Rows matching the key's current content.

unmatched_count.description: Screening (E9b): delivered records with no active score reaching `review_low` — genuinely new as far as the model can tell.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time. Receipts were written once until E9b; the screening pass now updates the row after the match stage, because the verdicts do not exist until the run has scored.

Job.description: A unit of work on the dispatcher's queue: its kind, params, lifecycle state and retry bookkeeping.

clear_number.description: Incremented by every clear; fences readiness verdicts composed before the clear. Read as COALESCE(clear_number, 0).

dataset_id.description: The dataset this job runs against. NULL only for org-level kinds (provision) — every lake-touching job carries it, and the per-dataset writer lock keys on it once the queue is re-scoped.

error_class.description: Why the job failed, as a class the UI can act on: precondition (an input is missing — expected during onboarding), transient_io (worth retrying), config (the tenant config is wrong), internal (a bug). Null until a failure.

error_detail.description: The failure's human text, already chain-flattened. Kept beside error_class so a steward sees the reason without reading pod logs.

id.description: The job's unique id (UUIDv7, minted at enqueue).

idempotency_key.description: Optional dedup key, unique per org.

image_digest.description: Image digest the planning dispatcher ran, so a deploy mid-run is legible.

kind.description: The job kind (run_all, correct, maintain, train, ...).

max_attempts.description: Vestigial: no statement consults it. It bounded the job-level retry that went with the legacy in-process arm (#645); the live budget is task_instances.max_tries, per attempt.

not_before.description: Earliest time the job may be claimed. A retry sets it to the backoff deadline.

org_id.description: The tenant this job runs for.

owner_epoch.description: The dispatcher process epoch that planned or adopted the run.

policy_hash.description: sha256 over the compiled DAG's per-node policy (retries, backoff, timeout, class, segment); a divergence proceeds with the diff logged.

run_id.description: The run this job produced, once dispatched.

schedule_id.description: The schedule that enqueued the job, if any.

state.description: Lifecycle state (queued, dispatching, running, succeeded, failed, canceling, canceled).

structural_fingerprint.description: sha256 over the compiled DAG's shape (names, versions, edges, trigger rules), written at planning; a clear or adoption refuses on mismatch (batch-orchestration-design §3.4).

updated_at.description: When the job row was last updated.

MatchingModel.description: An immutable version of a tenant's matching model: the settings document the engine scores against, its hash, provenance and activation state.

activated_at.description: When this version was activated, if it ever was.

dataset_id.description: The dataset whose corpus this model was trained for.

entity_type.description: Which canonical schema the model scores against; a model cannot be activated for a lake of the other entity type.

id.description: The version row's unique id (UUIDv7, minted when the version is created).

model_hash.description: SHA-256 of model_json, so a scored row can be tied back to the exact document that produced it.

model_json.description: The settings document the engine loads (comparison levels, their SQL, m/u probabilities, blocking rules). Stored as text, not jsonb, so it round-trips byte-exact — model_hash is taken over these bytes and the engine's determinism depends on them.

model_version_label.description: The identity stamped onto every row this model scores (match_scores.model_version, runs.model_version). It is NOT the version number: it must equal the model_version the frozen term-frequency snapshot CSV is keyed by, because the TF lookup joins on (model_version, tf_snapshot_id) and a mismatch silently returns no term frequencies — changing a pair's score rather than failing. Seeded from the org's ER_MODEL_VERSION; required when uploading a model, for the same reason.

name.description: The model's name within the tenant; versions are monotonic within a name, so one tenant can keep several models (a classic rule model beside a trained one) and switch between them.

org_id.description: The tenant this model version belongs to.

provenance.description: Where this version came from: the seeded starter file, a training run (corpus digest, args, seed), an authored upload, or the version it was derived from.

state.description: Draft until activated; exactly one version of a name is active at a time, and activating the next archives the previous. There is deliberately no partial unique index enforcing that: a single UPDATE that moves both rows can transiently violate a non-deferrable unique index even when the end state is legal, so activation is instead one atomic statement that cannot produce two actives, and the active read orders by version so a hypothetical second one could never be served silently.

tf_snapshot_id.description: The frozen term-frequency snapshot this model scores against, when it has one. Paired with model_version_label by the TF lookup.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

version.description: The monotonic version number within (org, name). Versions are immutable: a retrain or a weight override mints the next one rather than editing this.

MetricSnapshot.description: One run's resolution metrics, kept so the dashboard can show a TREND rather than only a current value. The dashboard has always computed its numbers live from the lake, which means it can say what is true now and nothing about whether that is better or worse than last week — which is the question an operator actually has.

auto_merge_pairs.description: Active scores at or above the auto-merge threshold.

captured_at.description: The run's logical clock, not wall time — so a replayed fixture produces the same snapshot.

duplicate_groups.description: Entities with more than one member.

duplicate_records.description: Records sitting in an entity with more than one member — the numerator of the duplicate rate. Counting GROUPS instead would call a 5-record cluster and a 2-record cluster the same amount of duplication.

entities.description: Entities the run resolved them into.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('metric_snapshots:' || run_id).

largest_group.description: Members in the biggest entity. A sudden jump here is the signature of an over-merge, which an average cluster size hides completely.

review_backlog.description: Open review items after the run — the work the thresholds are handing to humans.

review_band_pairs.description: Active scores in the gray band: scored, not merged. The two together say where the thresholds are actually sitting.

run_id.description: The run these metrics describe. One snapshot per run, so a re-run of the same id overwrites rather than double-counting.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time.

MetricSnapshotSource.description: One run's duplicate attribution, per source system. The corpus-wide duplicate rate says a tenant has a problem; it does not say WHERE the problem comes from, and the answer is nearly always one feed. Retained per run beside metric_snapshots for the same reason that table exists: a live number says what is true now and nothing about whether a source is getting better or worse.

captured_at.description: The run's logical timestamp, duplicated here so the series is readable without joining.

contributed_groups.description: How many duplicate groups contain at least one of this source's records. A source can account for few duplicate RECORDS while touching many groups, which is the signature of a feed that adds one bad row to everything rather than one bad batch.

duplicate_records.description: How many of them share an entity with at least one other record — counted by RECORD rather than by group, the same judgement metric_snapshots made: counting groups calls a five-record cluster and a pair the same amount of duplication.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('metric_snapshot_sources:' || run_id || ':' || source_system).

records.description: How many of this source's records are in the corpus.

run_id.description: The run this attribution describes; shares its id with the metric_snapshots row.

updated_at.description: Last-update stamp; a re-run of the same run_id corrects rather than appends.

Org.description: A tenant: its config pointer, lake env, lifecycle state and active config version.

active_config_version.description: The currently published config version, if any.

config_path.description: Path to the tenant's config document.

drop_root.description: Optional object-store root for tenant purge.

env.description: Lake connection env (catalog, data path, metadata schema).

id.description: The tenant's unique id (UUIDv7, minted at creation).

max_concurrent_jobs.description: How many of this org's jobs may be active at once, across its datasets (the noisy-neighbor cap). NULL inherits the server default (ER_ORG_JOB_CAP, which ships as 1 — the pre-dataset single-writer profile). The per-DATASET writer lock is separate and absolute.

name.description: The tenant's unique name (the routing handle; URLs stay name-based).

s3_ingest_bucket.description: Bucket the auto-ingest poller watches for this tenant. Null means auto-ingest is off, which is every existing tenant — the feature has to be opted into, because a poller that starts reading a bucket nobody pointed at it would be ingesting data on its own initiative.

s3_ingest_prefix.description: Key prefix under `s3_ingest_bucket`, with one directory per config source beneath it. A column rather than a key in `env` deliberately: `env` is handed to the engine subprocess, while this is read by the control plane itself, and D5 is what happens when the two stores of per-tenant settings disagree.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

PairLabel.description: A human (or model) verdict on one candidate pair — the training signal the engine has always been able to learn from and never had. One row per (org, pair): a re-label corrects the previous verdict rather than stacking another.

created_at.description: When the verdict was first recorded.

dataset_id.description: The dataset whose record pair this verdict is about — record keys are lake-local.

id.description: UUIDv7, minted by the application.

labeled_by.description: The actor that recorded the verdict.

model_version.description: The model whose score prompted this label, when there was one. Null for a label recorded without a score in front of it.

note.description: Optional free text from the labeller.

org_id.description: The tenant whose corpus the pair belongs to; every read is scoped by it.

origin.description: Where the verdict came from. `human` is an explicit labelling session; `reviewer` is implicit feedback from resolving a review item; `llm` is a model's suggestion. Kept apart so training can weight or exclude a source, and so an accuracy number can say whose labels it was measured against.

rec_a_key.description: The pair's lower record key, canonical order — the same ordering match_scores uses, so a label and a score describe the same pair.

rec_b_key.description: The pair's higher record key, canonical order.

score_at_label.description: The match probability shown to the labeller, so a later accuracy pass can tell what the model thought at the time rather than what it thinks now.

updated_at.description: When it was last corrected.

verdict.description: Whether these two records are the same entity. Deliberately binary: a labeller who is unsure should skip rather than guess, because a guessed label trains the model on noise and is indistinguishable afterwards from a confident one.

ProfileFinding.description: One coded observation a profile made about a corpus — a column mostly null, a blocking key dominated by one value, a record id that is not unique. Stored rather than derived at read time because the thresholds that produced a finding belong to the run that applied them: re-deriving later against changed thresholds would silently rewrite history, and a finding is the part of a profile a user is most likely to act on.

code.description: The finding's registry code (P001, P002, …). Codes are append-only and a retired rule keeps its code, so a stored finding stays interpretable after the rule that made it is gone — which is the point of coding them rather than storing only prose.

column_name.description: The column the finding is about, or the empty string for a dataset-level finding (a duplicate row rate, a schema change). A sentinel rather than NULL because this column is in the natural key, and a NULL key column never matches in a MERGE's ON clause — every re-profile would insert a second copy of the same finding.

detail.description: The measurements behind the message — the shares, counts and thresholds — so a consumer can chart or re-check a finding without re-reading the column profile. NULL for a finding whose message is already complete.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('profile_findings:' || profile_run_id || ':' || code || ':' || column_name).

message.description: The finding in one human sentence, with its numbers already in it. Rendered rather than templated at read time because the numbers are what make it actionable, and a message assembled later could be assembled against different data than the one that triggered it.

profile_run_id.description: The profile run that produced this finding. Named for the relation it points at, per the foreign-key convention; no `references` is declared because DuckLake enforces no foreign keys (V11).

severity.description: How much the finding should interrupt: `error`, `warning` or `info`. Carried on the row rather than looked up from the registry so that a severity reclassification does not retroactively change what a past profile reported.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time.

ProfileRun.description: One execution of the dataset profiler over one corpus stage, and the cache key for its result. A profile exists to be looked at repeatedly and compared against the previous delivery, so recomputing it on every view would make the cheap tier expensive for no new information.

captured_at.description: The run's logical clock, not wall time — so a replayed fixture produces the same row.

column_count.description: Columns profiled. Read with row_count it says how wide the scan was, which is the only honest predictor of what a re-profile will cost.

config_hash.description: The config version in force when the profile ran, so a finding about a blocking rule can be traced to the rule set it was judged against. NULL for a profile that predates any published config — the common case for a first delivery, which is exactly when profiling is most useful.

corpus_digest.description: A content digest of the rows profiled, and the actual cache key: one hash per row over all its columns, summed (so row order does not matter) and folded together with the row count. Equal digest means equal data, which is the question a cache has to answer — unlike the lake snapshot, which also moves when something unrelated is written, including this profile itself. Computed in one extra scan, which is cheap beside the distinct counts and top-k the profile already pays for.

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock cost of the profile, kept so the decision to run a deeper tier can be made from a measurement rather than a guess.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('profile_runs:' || subject || ':' || source_system || ':' || corpus_digest || ':' || tier).

ingest_batch_id.description: For a `raw` subject profiled automatically as a delivery lands, the delivery it describes — which lets drift be read between two consecutive batches. Provenance and ONLY provenance: this described itself as the per-delivery cache key until the auto-profile was built, and it was neither, because the key is `corpus_digest` and nothing populated this column at all. The digest is the better key anyway — two deliveries carrying identical content share it, where keying on the batch recomputes the same answer for every redelivery of an unchanged file. NULL for the standardized and golden subjects, which describe the whole corpus rather than one landing, and NULL for a profile an operator or a schedule asked for, which describes whatever is landed now rather than one batch.

model_version.description: The model whose rules a tier-2 or tier-3 profile measured, when one existed. NULL is the normal case for a new corpus and is not a defect: the candidate-key estimates are deliberately computable without a model.

row_count.description: Rows the profile actually read, which is the sampled count when sampling was on. Named row_count rather than rows because `rows` is reserved in DuckDB and a column called that cannot be selected unquoted.

sample_proportion.description: The sampled share of rows, NULL when the whole corpus was read.

sample_seed.description: The salt the deterministic sample was drawn with, NULL when unsampled. Recorded because the sample is reproducible only if the seed is known, and a profile nobody can redraw cannot be compared against its successor.

sampled.description: Whether the figures come from a sample. Stored as its own flag rather than inferred from sample_proportion, because a consumer rendering a number has to know whether it is exact before it decides how to label it.

snapshot.description: The DuckLake snapshot version the profile was computed against — informational provenance, deliberately NOT the cache key. It cannot be: the snapshot counter is per-catalog and this profile's own write advances it, so keying on it means every profile invalidates itself and the stored result grows a duplicate on every view instead of being reused. Found by the e2e test that asserts two profiles of unchanged data are one row.

source_system.description: The source whose delivered rows were profiled, or `*` when the subject is not source-scoped. A sentinel rather than NULL because this column is part of the natural key, and NULL never equals NULL in a MERGE's ON clause — a nullable key column would miss every match and insert a duplicate profile on each run.

subject.description: Which stage of the corpus was profiled: `raw` (as delivered, per source), `standardized` (the canonical attributes), or `golden` (post-resolution). The same aggregates run over all three, which is why a post-resolution profile costs no new machinery. Not an accepted_values list because DuckLake enforces no CHECK constraints (V11) and declaring one would promise a guarantee no layer provides.

tier.description: Profiling depth: 1 shape (one aggregate pass), 2 entity-resolution readiness (blocking cost, skew, coverage), 3 model readiness (agreement rates, u-probability pre-flight). Kept in the key so a cheap profile is never mistaken for a deep one, and so asking for tier 3 does not read a tier 1 row and report it as complete.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time. A re-profile of an unchanged snapshot rewrites the row in place rather than appending, so this moves while the rest of the row does not.

RecordQuality.description: A per-record data-quality score, 0-100, with the three dimensions kept separately. The dimensions are kept because a single number says a record is bad and not what to do about it: complete-but-invalid, valid-but-empty and simply old are three different jobs.

completeness.description: Weighted fraction of the configured attributes that are populated.

freshness.description: 1.0 within `fresh_days` of the run, decaying to 0.0 at `stale_days`. NULL when the source carries no timestamp, because unknown age is not the same as old.

id.description: Content-derived row id: sha256('record_qualities:' || record_key).

score.description: 0-100, the weighted mean of the dimensions that APPLY to this record. A dimension that cannot be judged is left out of the mean rather than counted as zero.

updated_at.description: Run-logical last-write time.

validity.description: Fraction of the PRESENT validatable fields that passed standardization. NULL when the record has none of them — a record with no email is already penalised by completeness, and scoring its validity zero would penalise the same absence twice.

S3IngestCursor.description: What the auto-ingest poller has already read, one row per (org, source). The poller runs on every dispatcher tick and the newest object under a prefix stays the newest until a new one arrives, so without this row the same CSV would be re-ingested every few seconds forever — an unbounded run loop over the tenant's own lake. An upsert rather than a log: the question it answers is 'what is already in', not 'what has ever been in', and the audit log already answers the second.

created_at.description: When this source was first auto-ingested.

dataset_id.description: The dataset the polled source lands in.

delivery_id.description: The delivery this object became, tying the cursor to the audit row and the run it enqueued.

etag.description: The object's ETag when it was read. The reason this column exists: a tenant who overwrites `crm/daily.csv` with new content leaves the key identical, so a key-only cursor would never read the new rows. Nullable because a listing can omit it.

id.description: UUIDv7, minted by the application.

object_key.description: The full S3 key of the object last ingested, kept whole so a tenant asking 'which file produced this run' gets the answer rather than a reconstruction.

org_id.description: The tenant whose prefix was polled; every read is scoped by it.

size_bytes.description: The object's size at ingest, so a later shrink is visible as one.

source.description: The config source this object landed as — the first path segment under the tenant's prefix.

updated_at.description: When it was last auto-ingested.

Schedule.description: A recurring job schedule for a tenant: its kind, cron and source.

dataset_id.description: The dataset this schedule enqueues for.

id.description: The schedule's unique id.

kind.description: The job kind the schedule enqueues.

last_enqueued_at.description: When the schedule last enqueued a job.

org_id.description: The tenant this schedule runs for.

source.description: What created the schedule (api, config:correction_pass, system:lake_maintain).

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

StagedStewardAction.description: A steward action staged for review/apply: its payload, state and outcome.

applied_at.description: When the action was applied, if it has been.

dataset_id.description: The dataset whose lake this action drains into.

error.description: The failure reason, if the action failed.

id.description: The staged action's unique id.

org_id.description: The tenant the action applies to.

state.description: Whether the action is pending, applied or failed.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

Tag.description: A tenant's own label for entities and review groups: the vocabulary a steward sorts work by.

active.description: Whether the tag is in use. Retiring is a soft delete: `taggings` references this row, every foreign key in this schema is NO ACTION, and a hard DELETE would therefore fail for exactly the tags that had been used — which is the bug D11 found in webhooks. Keeping the row also keeps the history legible: what a group was once marked as is part of why it was handled the way it was.

apply_min_role.description: The minimum role allowed to apply or unapply this tag. Null means the route default (steward). Finer than the route's role check because a tag can name a decision only an admin should be able to mark — the spec's per-tag permission.

created_by.description: The actor that created the tag.

description.description: What the tag means, for the steward who inherits it. Null when nobody wrote one.

id.description: The tag's unique id (UUIDv7, minted by the application).

kind.description: Who the tag belongs to. `user` is the steward's vocabulary; `system` is reserved for tags the platform itself writes (merge, manual_merge, unmatch, link, split) — a system tag cannot be retired through the API, and its name cannot be taken by a user tag, so the two vocabularies can never collide.

name.description: The label a steward sees and types. Unique per tenant among active tags, because two tags with one name make a filter ambiguous and a bulk action unsafe.

org_id.description: The tenant that owns the tag. A tag is never shared across tenants: it names one tenant's own workflow.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time.

Tagging.description: One tag applied to one subject: the attachment, kept apart from the tag so retiring a tag does not rewrite what it was applied to.

created_by.description: The actor that applied the tag. Kept because tagging is how work is assigned, so who claimed it matters.

dataset_id.description: The dataset whose subject this tag is applied to — subject ids are lake-local.

id.description: The tagging's unique id (UUIDv7, minted by the application).

org_id.description: The tenant. Denormalised from the tag so every read is scoped by one predicate rather than a join — the same reason every other tenant-scoped relation carries it.

subject_id.description: The entity id or review id. Deliberately NOT a foreign key: an entity lives in the lake and a review is rebuilt by every reconcile, so a database-level reference would be to a row this store does not own. A tagging whose subject has gone is harmless — it reads as absent and is cleaned up by nothing, which is the honest cost of tagging something another store owns.

subject_type.description: What was tagged: `entity` (a resolved cluster, by its entity id) or `review` (an open review item). Two kinds rather than two tables, because a filter and a bulk action want one list of 'things tagged X' and a union of two relations would make every such read a join.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time.

TaskInstance.description: One try of one task of one job (Airflow's task_instance shape): the live try has live = TRUE, archived tries have live NULL and stay in the table as history (batch-orchestration-design §4.2).

archived_reason.description: Why the row stopped being live; NULL while live. retry = archive_try, cleared = a terminal row rotated by clear, restarted = a clear-while-live rotation (complete_restart). Pending rows reset by a clear are not archived (no try was consumed).

counters.description: Progress counters, replaced on every heartbeat and at finish.

dataset_id.description: Copied from the job at planning (NULL for org-level jobs); the per-dataset pod lock keys on it once the executor is re-scoped.

error_class.description: er-errors' seven classes plus the executor's four.

escalated_from.description: Class of the OOMKilled predecessor try, so a mixed-class run is legible.

exit_code.description: Container exit code: the pod's own on finish, the watch's observation on record_evidence. Evidence for the row, never a classifier input (§6.5).

id.description: er_ids::natural_id('task_instances', [job_id, task_id, try_number]): a pure function of the attempt key, so the Job name is one too.

image_digest.description: Image digest this try ran, so a deploy mid-run is legible.

input.description: The work order: pinned upstream references, the RunPlan, params. Written whole by mark_scheduled at every readiness verdict (never merged), by advance_segment for a fused member, and copied by the retry insert; NULL on a none row.

k8s_job_name.description: batch/v1 Job name, `er-t-{20 hex of id}-l{launches}`, of the Job that ran this try; for a fused non-head member, the segment head's Job (advance_segment copies it).

kind.description: Where the body runs: a Kubernetes Job, or a dispatcher-local body under the control-task contract (§3.6).

launches.description: Infrastructure budget consumed by this try: Job creates whose pod never ran user code, plus disruptions while running; 1 for a member advanced inside a running segment pod.

live.description: TRUE on the live try, NULL once archived (NULLs are distinct, so the partial unique index admits one live row per coordinate).

max_tries.description: Cumulative try budget (Airflow max_tries): retries at planning; previous_try_number + retries after a clear. Eligible to retry while try_number <= max_tries.

next_resource_class.description: Operator override recorded by clear on a restarting row; complete_restart applies it to the successor.

not_before.description: Backoff deadline for up_for_retry; a short capacity wait for scheduled.

output.description: The serialized DurableOutput (a LakeRef or Plan), written at finish.

owner_epoch.description: The dispatcher process epoch (UUIDv7 minted at start) that claimed the launch; adoption rewrites it.

pod_name.description: Pod that ran this try, from the pod's bound token on first contact; cross-checked by the watch.

pod_uid.description: Pod UID, recorded from the token's claim; the watch confirms it.

resource_class.description: Class this try runs at; NULL for a control task. OOM escalation writes a larger class on the next try.

segment.description: Fusion segment id resolved at planning; NULL for a task that runs alone.

seq.description: Topological position from assembly; display and claim order.

snapshot_end.description: Lake snapshot of the task's last commit: the durable reference downstream pins to.

snapshot_start.description: Lake snapshot before the task's first commit.

state.description: Closed state set (§5). restarting and canceling are the write-ahead markers for clear and cancel of a live row.

teardown.description: Claimable while the job is canceling (finish).

termination_reason.description: Platform evidence, distinct from error_class, free text: OOMKilled, Evicted, DeadlineExceeded, Unschedulable, no_pod_created, vanished, quota, sigterm, sigkill, fenced, stale_start, structural_mismatch, build_skew, control_plane_unreachable, no_terminal_record, heartbeat_timeout, dispatcher_restart, revoked, and kin.

trace_context.description: traceparent of this try's span, a child of jobs.trace_context.

trigger_rule.description: Copied from the compiled graph at planning so the UI can explain propagation; the graph is the authority.

try_number.description: 1-based try. A new row per try.

updated_at.description: Row updated.

upstream.description: Upstream task_ids, a UI projection of the compiled edges.

Webhook.description: A tenant webhook endpoint: its URL, subscribed events and signing secret.

dataset_id.description: Optional dataset filter: NULL subscribes to every dataset's events.

id.description: The webhook's unique id.

org_id.description: The tenant that owns the webhook.

updated_at.description: Wall-clock last-write time (database default; advanced by mutations once the entity migrates).

WebhookDelivery.description: One attempt-tracked delivery of one event to one subscriber. The event is recorded here BEFORE any network call, so a subscriber that is briefly unreachable gets the event late instead of never.

attempt.description: Attempts handed out. Counted when claimed, not when reported, so a drainer that dies still consumes one.

created_at.description: When the event was recorded, which is before any delivery was attempted.

dataset_id.description: The dataset the delivered event came from, when it has one (provenance).

delivered_at.description: When a 2xx was received; NULL unless state is delivered.

error.description: Why the last attempt did not deliver: a transport error, or the outbound-URL guard's refusal.

id.description: UUIDv7, minted by the application.

max_attempts.description: Attempts before giving up. Six with the backoff below spans about ten minutes.

next_attempt_at.description: When this becomes claimable. NULL means immediately; set to a backoff in the future after a retryable failure.

org_id.description: The tenant whose subscriber this is for; every read is scoped by it.

payload.description: The exact body to POST. Stored rather than rebuilt so a retry delivers the same bytes the signature was computed over, and so the log shows what was actually sent.

response_code.description: The subscriber's HTTP status, when the POST completed at all.

state.description: pending until a drain settles it; delivered on a 2xx; failed when retries are exhausted or the destination is refused outright.

updated_at.description: Last write.
